subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The temperature 'danger zone' in which bacteria multiply most readily is approximately:
questions.explain: Between about 5 and 63 degrees C bacteria multiply rapidly, so foods should not be held there.

questions.q: Lactose intolerance occurs because the person:
options: Lacks sufficient lactase enzyme to digest milk sugar
questions.explain: Without enough lactase, lactose is not digested, causing bloating and discomfort.

questions.q: Freezing preserves food by:
options: Lowering water activity and temperature so micro-organisms cannot multiply
questions.explain: Freezing makes water unavailable and lowers temperature so micro-organisms become dormant, not dead.

questions.q: The Maillard reaction responsible for the brown crust on roast meat is a reaction between:
questions.explain: The Maillard reaction is non-enzymic browning between amino acids and reducing sugars on heating.

questions.q: Which best describes glycogen?
options: A storage polysaccharide of glucose found in the liver and muscles
questions.explain: Glycogen is the body's storage carbohydrate, a branched polymer of glucose units.

questions.q: The browning of toast surfaces and the dry crust of bread is mainly due to:
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the breakdown of starch to dextrins by dry heat, giving a brown colour.

questions.q: A person with coeliac disease must avoid:
options: Gluten found in wheat, barley and rye
questions.explain: Coeliac disease is an immune reaction to gluten, so wheat, barley and rye must be avoided.

questions.q: 'Food security' is best defined as:
options: Selling food at a high price
All people having reliable access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food
questions.explain: Food security means everyone has consistent access to enough safe, nutritious food for a healthy life.

questions.q: Modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) extends shelf life mainly by:
options: Heating the food in the pack
Altering the gases around the food to slow spoilage
questions.explain: MAP changes the proportions of gases (e.g. reducing oxygen) to slow microbial and chemical spoilage.

questions.q: Which is essential for stabilising a foam such as whisked egg-white meringue?
options: Partially denatured protein trapping air in a network
questions.explain: Whisking partly denatures egg protein, which stabilises the trapped air bubbles forming a foam.

questions.q: Listeria monocytogenes is of special concern because, unlike most pathogens, it can:
questions.explain: Listeria can multiply slowly at fridge temperatures, posing a risk in chilled ready-to-eat foods.

questions.q: Which is a cultural or religious factor that may influence food choice?
options: A sudden change in market price
questions.explain: Religious and cultural beliefs, such as vegetarianism or fasting, strongly shape what people choose to eat.

questions.q: In bread-making, the biological raising of the dough is produced by:
options: Yeast fermenting sugars to release carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Yeast ferments sugars, producing carbon dioxide that makes bread dough rise.

questions.q: Which carbohydrate is a monosaccharide?
questions.explain: Glucose is a single-sugar unit, whereas sucrose, lactose and maltose are disaccharides.

questions.q: Caramelisation differs from the Maillard reaction because it involves:
options: A reaction of proteins with sugars
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar alone when heated, without amino acids.

questions.q: Which pathogen is particularly associated with undercooked poultry and is a leading cause of food poisoning in the UK?
questions.explain: Campylobacter, often from raw or undercooked poultry, is the most common bacterial cause of UK food poisoning.

questions.q: By UK law, which information must legally appear on most pre-packed food labels?
options: A list of ingredients in descending order of weight
questions.explain: Ingredients must be listed by descending weight, alongside allergens, durability dates and other required details.

questions.q: Type-2 diabetes is characterised by:
options: The body's cells becoming resistant to insulin
Complete absence of insulin from birth
questions.explain: In type-2 diabetes cells become resistant to insulin, so blood glucose is poorly controlled.

questions.q: Which type of fatty acid contains no carbon-to-carbon double bonds?
questions.explain: Saturated fatty acids have all carbon bonds filled with hydrogen and no double bonds.

questions.q: Antioxidant nutrients such as vitamins A, C and E help the body by:
options: Neutralising free radicals and limiting cell damage
questions.explain: Antioxidants quench free radicals, reducing oxidative damage linked to chronic disease.

questions.q: Which mineral is most associated with the prevention of iron-deficiency anaemia?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; a deficiency causes anaemia.

questions.q: Preservation by canning relies mainly on which principle?
options: Adding acid to lower the pH
Lowering the temperature to slow bacteria
High-temperature heat treatment to destroy micro-organisms and sealing to prevent re-contamination
Removing oxygen by modified atmosphere only
questions.explain: Canning uses heat to destroy micro-organisms and an airtight seal to keep the food sterile.

questions.q: Which group of people has an increased requirement for iron and folate?
questions.explain: Pregnancy raises iron needs for increased blood volume and folate to prevent neural tube defects.

questions.q: Salting and sugaring preserve foods primarily by:
options: Reducing the water activity available to micro-organisms
questions.explain: High salt or sugar concentrations draw water out by osmosis, lowering aw and inhibiting microbes.

questions.q: Gelatinisation occurs when:
options: Amino acids react with reducing sugars
Sugar is heated until it browns
Starch granules absorb liquid and swell on heating, thickening the mixture
Fat and water are mixed with an emulsifier
questions.explain: On heating in liquid, starch granules absorb water, swell and burst, thickening the sauce.

questions.q: Which vitamins are fat-soluble?
options: Vitamins A, D, E and K
questions.explain: Vitamins A, D, E and K dissolve in fat and can be stored in the body's fatty tissues.

questions.q: Which is the basic structural unit of a triglyceride?
options: Three glycerols and one fatty acid
One glycerol and three fatty acids
One glucose and three fatty acids
Three amino acids and one glycerol
questions.explain: A triglyceride consists of one glycerol molecule esterified with three fatty acids.

questions.q: Osteoporosis is most directly linked to a long-term deficiency of:
questions.explain: Inadequate calcium and vitamin D reduce bone mineral density, leading to brittle bones.

questions.q: Which factor would increase an adult's basal metabolic rate?
options: A greater proportion of lean muscle mass
questions.explain: Lean muscle is metabolically active, so a higher muscle mass raises BMR.

questions.q: Which raising agent works by producing carbon dioxide when it reacts with an acid and moisture?
questions.explain: Baking powder contains bicarbonate of soda and an acid that release CO2 to aerate mixtures.
